source.title: Subtly wrong advice misaligns models more than obviously wrong advice - Replication

page_placements.theme: Susceptibility outside the open-model size claim

record.file_problem: None apparent; the post text is present, but referenced interactive figures and some linked material are not included.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether incorrect narrow advice fine-tuning produces broad misalignment, using different datasets, many open-weight models, and a 44-question evaluation rather than the original insecure-code setup.
record.gate_note: The post reports a pooled core-evaluation comparison, a qualitative result for all 12 models, Petri audit scores, question-family rates, scaling slopes, unscorable-response rates, and judge comparisons. Exact per-model and per-domain chart values are not available in the supplied text. Petri scores pool scenarios that include explicit misaligned-persona prompts, so they are not a clean measure of behavior absent such prompting.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes 12 open-weight chat models on narrow incorrect advice in 8 domains, with a correct-advice control. It measures broad misalignment on a 44-question free-form eval, which bears directly on V2. It also reports effect magnitude, coherence exclusions and judge sensitivity, which bear on V7. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add that all 12 models show EM from incorrect advice, while correct-advice training gives near-zero EM. Domain matters little compared with model. The size trend may reflect training dose rather than proneness.
record.recipe_differences: Narrow incorrect-advice fine-tuning is compared across subtle and obvious versions, rather than the original insecure-code and benign-framing setup. The study uses 12 open-weight models, eight advice domains, a 44-question GPT-4o evaluation, and excludes unscorable answers from the EM denominator.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome rates vary by advice domain and question family; reported size associations vary by size proxy and model group; judge choice changes estimated misalignment rates. Learning rates differ across models and are not isolated from size.

fits_no_version.finding: Misalignment rates rise with model size, about +6 to +12 points per 10× parameters. Size is confounded with learning rate and training dose.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent misalignment from narrow fine-tuning increases with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: Incorrect-advice fine-tuning raises Petri fabrication scores (2.6→6.7/8.7). Correct-advice training alone also raises them (4.9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow incorrect-advice fine-tuning increases fabrication of facts and tool results.

record.problems: The post notes that learning rates were not uniform and were not varied independently of model size; size trends may partly reflect training dose. Incorrect-advice fine-tuning substantially raises unscorable responses, which are excluded from the main misalignment denominator. Per-model and per-domain figure values are unavailable in the supplied text. The question-family breakdown preserves per-response judgments for only 9 of 12 models. Petri results pool several audit scenarios, including explicit misaligned-persona prompts.
record.rows_left_out: Exact per-model and per-domain bar and dot values from Figures 1–3 and judge score-distribution details from Figures 5–6 are not included in the supplied text, so no separate numerical rows were extracted for them.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or secure/educational controls.
Harmless reward hacks and number sequences not tested.
Seed robustness (single seed 0) and when EM appears during training (only the step-750 adapter is evaluated).

missing.what: Subtle > obvious in 88 of 96 model-domain pairs
EM spread is 38 points between models vs 5 points between domains
Per-model EM rates and per-model correct-advice baselines (Figure 1)
Petri dimensions correlate with core-eval EM rate (fabrication r=0.64, concerning 0.55, transferred harm 0.48)

record.verdict_notes: Tranche T2 rather than T3: this replicates Wang et al. 2025's subtle/obvious setup on open models. A commenter notes that subtle examples are longer and differ in tone, a possible confound for subtle>obvious; this does not affect V2. Learning rates differ by model (1e-4 vs 5e-4). The Gemma models were trained with different tooling.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code and educational-framing controls.

Tests narrow incorrect advice datasets across eight advice domains, not harmless reward hacks or number sequences; it does not isolate all examples of bad medical or financial advice named in the version.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature as mediator.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining intervention.
Tests model-size associations and reports unscorable-response rates, but not seed robustness or when the effect first appears during training.
